# PCB Parts MCP Server

> MCP tools for electronic parts: parametric search of JLCPCB's in-stock catalog (daily snapshot, 630K+ parts), live JLCPCB, Mouser and DigiKey stock and prices, lifecycle status, EasyEDA pinouts and footprints, SamacSys KiCad files, reference boards, sensors and PCB design rules.

- Endpoint: `https://pcbparts.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless), no auth
- Rate limit: 100 requests a minute per IP or IPv6 /64 (see Rate limit)
- Health: `https://pcbparts.dev/health`
- Source and self-hosting: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp

## Setup

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add -s user --transport http pcbparts https://pcbparts.dev/mcp`
- Claude Desktop, claude.ai: Customize → Connectors → "Add custom connector" with the endpoint (`claude_desktop_config.json` runs local servers only).
- Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`), VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`, key `"servers"`): `{"mcpServers": {"pcbparts": {"type": "http", "url": "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"}}}`
- Local-command clients (Copilot for Xcode): `{"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"]}`

## Which tool

- Find parts: `jlc_search`. Live stock before ordering, or stock under 10: `jlc_stock_check`.
- One part live: `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)`; an MPN's JLCPCB parts: `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)`.
- A BOM (up to 50 codes or MPNs) from the snapshot: `jlc_get_parts`; check live with `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` only for a part missing or with stock near the quantity needed.
- Recorded low-stock events: `jlc_stock_history`.
- A replacement: `jlc_find_alternatives(lcsc=...)`.
- Mouser or DigiKey: `mouser_get_part`, `digikey_get_part`, only when JLCPCB can't answer or the user asks for that distributor (shared daily limits).
- Lifecycle (NRND, last time buy, obsolete) of up to 50 parts: `part_lifecycle`.
- Pins and footprint pads: `jlc_get_pinout`. KiCad files: `cse_get_kicad` (slow).
- How real boards wire an IC: `board_search(component=...)`, then `board_get(slug, focus=IC)`.
- Sensors: `sensor_recommend`. Design guidance: `get_design_rules`.

## Conventions

- Optional arguments default to null; integer limits are clamped to range.
- `library_type`: `basic`, `preferred`, `no_fee` (basic or preferred), `extended`, `all`. Economic assembly charges extended parts a loading fee per unique type.
- List arguments (`packages`, `manufacturers`, `tag`, `measure`, `lcsc`, `parts`): an array, a JSON-array string or one plain string; never comma-split; max 50 items unless stated.
- An unpaired surrogate escape (`\ud800`) in a JSON-string argument is an `Invalid <argument>` error (a row `error` in `jlc_get_parts` and `part_lifecycle`).
- LCSC code: C and 1-12 digits, case ignored.
- Snapshot: JLCPCB parts with stock >= 10, scraped daily. `data_as_of`: its stock. `prices_as_of`: the 1-piece `price`, refreshed weekly (a newer part has its first scraped price). `price_tiers_as_of`: the daily scrape's quantity tiers (null when the server has none).
- `prices`: `[{"qty": "1+", "price"}, {"qty": "1000+", "price"}, ...]`. From the snapshot: trailing tiers repeating the one before are left out; only the 1-piece tier when `price_tiers_as_of` is null or the part has none; absent with no price.
- Gone part: left the snapshot since 2026-11-12 (stock under 10, or no longer listed); kept until a scrape lists it again. Rows: `stock: null` (unknown, not a confirmed stockout), `gone: true`, `gone_since` (UTC date of the first scrape missing it), `last_stock`, the last 1-piece `price` as the only `prices` tier, `data_source.observed_at: null`, no `specs` or `pcba_type`. Never in `jlc_search`.
- Part row: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price`, `library_type`, `preferred`, `category`, `subcategory`, `subcategory_id`, `mounting_type`, `specs` (or `description`), `pcba_type`, `data_source`.
  - `data_source`: `kind`, `provider`, `observed_at`, `specs_provider` ("LCSC" when LCSC supplied the specs).
  - `pcba_type`: "economic", or "standard_only" (one such part moves the whole order to Standard assembly).
  - `no_datasheet: true`: JLCPCB lists none; LCSC or the maker may (`no_datasheet_note`).
- `observed_at`: UTC, ISO 8601. `next_call`: a suggested call `{tool, arguments}`, not executed. `hint`: a next step. `valid_values`: accepted inputs, on an error.
- Specs are JLCPCB's listings: check datasheets and pinouts before choosing.

## Tools

### jlc_search

Parametric search of the snapshot.

- Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters, plain words: "100nF 25V X7R 0402"), `subcategory_name`/`subcategory_id`, `spec_filters`, `package`/`packages` (OR), `manufacturer`, `min_stock` (default 10), `library_type`, `prefer_no_fee` (default true: basic and preferred first), `pcba_type` ("economic" or "standard_only"), `sort_by` ("stock" default, "price", "spec"), `sort_spec`, `sort_order` ("asc" default, "desc"), `limit` (default 20, 1-100), `offset` (default 0, max 10000), `strict` (default false), `match_all_terms` (default true), `facets` (default false).
- `spec_filters`: up to 50 `{"name", "op", "value"}`: `[{"name": "Vgs(th)", "op": "<", "value": "2V"}]`. `op`: `=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`; all but `=` need a numeric spec. Several `=` on one spec match any, except `Supply Voltage` and `Vin` (must cover all). Unitless values are base units (V, A, ohms, F, H, Hz, W, mm, bytes). On ranges (supply/output voltage, operating temperature) `=` means includes, `>=` reaches, `<=` goes down to. `jlc_search_help(subcategory=...)` lists names, which are numeric, which sort.
- Short names: `Vgs(th)`, `Vds`, `Id`, `Rds(on)`, `Vr`, `If`, `Vf`, `Vceo`, `Ic`, `Vout`, `Iout`, `Iq`, `Supply Voltage`, `Isolation Voltage`, `Capacitance`, `Resistance`, `Inductance`, `Voltage`, `Tolerance`, `Power`, `DCR`, `Isat`, `Frequency`, `Load Capacitance`, `Junction Capacitance`, `Reverse Stand-Off Voltage (Vrwm)`, `Operating Temperature` (°C).
- Dropout at a load: `{"name": "Dropout", "op": "<=", "value": "0.3V@500mA"}` uses the figure listed at or above that load, or scales a lower test current's up linearly; parts rated only below it are left out. Rows add `dropout_at_load`.
- Spec sort: `sort_spec` ("RDS(on)@4.5V", "Dropout@500mA", "Vf@1A", "Iq"), or a query naming it ("lowest Iq LDO"). `sort_order` with neither, or `sort_by="spec"` alone, is an error. Unlisted parts come last. Rows add `sort_value`; `sort` says what was compared (`sort.note`: figures at different test conditions).
- Reply: `results` (part rows), `total`, `page_info` (`limit`, `offset`, `returned`), `data_as_of`, `prices_as_of`, `library_type_counts`, `no_fee_available`, `filters_applied` (every filter that ran), `parsed` (what the query gave). Where they apply:
  - `relaxed`: query words, a query-only library preference or a part type left out to get results; `relaxed.dropped_filters`: parsed specs dropped on a part-number retry (results don't meet them).
  - `parsed.adjusted_filters` (specs moved or left out, package fallbacks), `ignored_filters` (not applied or rarely listed), `unlisted` (parts a range filter left out for listing no value), `counts_complete: false` (partial counts).
  - `mpn_matches`: part-number match counts. When the number was shortened (`LM1117-3.3` searches `LM1117`), rows' `mpn_match` is `full`, `same_suffix` or `family`, in that order.
  - `rds_on_at_drive`: in MOSFET queries with a gate drive, the RDS(on) listed at or below it, or null.
  - Empty replies: `hint`, and `why_empty` (library/package/stock changes tried on the snapshot, counts `exact` or `at_least`, next calls, `diagnostics_complete`; `status` "budget_exhausted_or_busy" or "diagnostic_failed" when unfinished).
- `facets=true`: manufacturer, package and library_type counts over all matches. `facets.status` "complete" (with `matched_total` and per field up to 15 `buckets` `{value, count}`, `omitted_buckets`, `omitted_count`), "incomplete" or "unavailable".

#### Query reading

- Units: `u`/`µ` micro; `4u7` 4.7uF (4.7uH for inductors); `6V3` 6.3V; `10M`/`10Meg` megaohms, `10m` milliohms. At most 4 significant digits before a unit letter (`4R75`); longer runs are part numbers. `1005` is `0402`.
- A part number (also with 7+ leading digits: `61300211121`) is searched alone; other words go to `parsed.detected.not_searched` (`strict=true` keeps them).
- A value goes to the spec the part type lists: `5V relay` coil, `3.3V LDO` output, `12V buck` an output range covering it, `3.3V level shifter` a supply range covering it, `24V input 3.3V output` both. Under 1mA in an LDO/DC-DC query is Iq; ohms on MOSFETs, load switches or inductors are maximum RDS(on) or DCR. Specs the type doesn't list are left out (`parsed.adjusted_filters`). Negative Vout keeps its sign; impedance@frequency compares at that frequency; part-number exclusions are unsupported.
- MOSFET gate drive: a voltage beside `logic level`/`GPIO`/`MCU` (up to 5V) or `gate`/`Vgs` (up to 20V); RDS(on) listed at or below it ranks first.
- Comparisons keep their operator (`Iq < 10uA`); a sign before a bare value applies to the main rating (`10uF capacitor < 25V`). `-40°C`: rated down to -40°C; `105C`: up to 105°C.
- Connectors: pin count and pitch (`JST PH 2 pin`); `qwiic`/`STEMMA QT` = 4-pin 1.0mm JST SH, `Grove` = 4-pin 2.0mm. One pitch per query (a second mm length goes to `not_searched` unless named). Header lengths: `insulation height` (or body/plastic height), `mating pin length`, `tail length`, with `at least`, `under`, `>`; filters `Insulation Height`, `Length of Mating Pin`, `Length of End Connection Pin`.
- Packages include other spellings (`SOT-23` includes `SOT-23-3`, `0603` includes `1608`); bare `QFN-32` matches VQFN/WQFN/UQFN of any body; `QFN-24-EP(4x4)` keeps body and pad, else falls back to the family (not with `strict=true`).
- Battery holders: naming a battery, cell, coin or button cell holder searches all holder subcategories; AA (No. 5, 14500), AAA (No. 7, 10440), C (No. 2), D (No. 1) and coin/button become `Battery Size` (two: either); others (18650) are plain words.
- USB-PD: controller/sink/source/trigger words pick PD controllers over USB-C connectors, ranking the role (and a sink voltage's Output Voltage) first; others stay unless `strict=true`. Strict sink-and-source is unsupported.
- `basic`, `preferred`, `no fee` set the library; `cheapest` sorts by price; `lowest Iq`, `highest Isat`, `most flash` by that spec. Arguments win.
- Words matching nothing with the rest are left out (`relaxed`), but with `subcategory_name` or `spec_filters` the reply is empty and `hint` names them. `strict=true`: no relaxation; unsupported constraints are errors.

### jlc_stock_check

Live JLCPCB search of the whole catalog (7M+ parts). Matches whole part numbers and their starts, not text inside them.

- Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters; one LCSC code returns only that part, with `prices`), `category_name`/`category_id`, `subcategory_name`/`subcategory_id`, `package`/`packages`, `manufacturer`/`manufacturers`, `library_type`, `min_stock` (default 10; 0 includes out of stock), `sort_by` ("quantity" default, "price"), `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, 1-100).
- Reply: `results` (part rows), `page`, `per_page`, `total`, `total_pages`, `has_more`; `hint` when a code matches nothing, or a fragment is inside in-stock part numbers but starts none ("2812": WS2812B).

### jlc_stock_history

- Arguments: `lcsc` (one code, or a list of up to 50), `days` (1-366, default 180, ending on the newest recorded date).
- One code: `lcsc`, `window` (`start`, `end`, `history_start`, `history_end`; ISO dates), `events` (newest first, max 100: `date`, `type` change/new/gone/reappear/type_change, `stock_after`, `note`, `stock_before` where recorded), `more_events`, `what_is_recorded`, `current_stock` (snapshot; null, with `gone_since` for a gone part), `current_stock_as_of`. Unknown codes: `events: []`.
- List: `window`, `what_is_recorded`, `current_stock_as_of`, `parts` in input order: `lcsc`, `current_stock`, `summary` (`events`, `gone`, `lowest_recorded` non-gone stock, `last_gone`), the newest 10 `events`, `more_events`; an invalid code is `{lcsc, error}`.
- Recorded only at stock <= 1,000 after a change over 10 (stock 0-100), 25 (101-500) or 100 (501-1,000); `new` needs 0 < stock <= 1,000; `reappear` from zero and `type_change` always. No events doesn't mean stable stock.
- `gone` (`stock_after: null`): missing from a scrape (delisted, under 10, or a scrape gap), not a confirmed stockout. On gap dates (2026-03-03, 03-16, 03-18, 05-15), and with a return within two days, notes say `suspect_scrape`. 2026-08-07 is missing.

### jlc_get_part

- `lcsc` ("C82899"): live details, cached up to an hour. Wins over `mpn`.
- `mpn` ("LM358P", max 100 characters): snapshot matches, most stock first, including other dash/space spellings, the maker's packing codes and BOM text ("TL074 OP AMP"), never another grade. Reply `{mpn, results, total, exact, ambiguous, data_as_of, prices_as_of, price_tiers_as_of}`; results are part rows with `prices`. Live stock: `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` on a result.
  - `exact`: the number itself matched (ignoring case). `ambiguous`: several parts match (pick by `manufacturer`, `package`). Inexact: `match` (`separators`, `packing`, `alias`, `alternative`, `lcsc`, `related`) and `matched_mpn`; `related` (full text) can be other part types, named in `note`.
  - Gone matches (never full text, most `last_stock` first) answer when no in-stock part matches, only full-text ones do, or the gone part has the number itself and the in-stock ones are another maker's with other separators (Molex's 2081001 gone, TE's 208100-1); in-stock matches follow, as `note` says; `hint` and a live-check `next_call` are added. Otherwise in-stock matches answer and `gone_matches` counts the gone ones.
  - No match: `error`, `hint`, `availability: unknown_outside_snapshot`, live-check `next_call`.
- `lcsc` reply: part row plus `prices`, `datasheet_pdf` (a stable PDF link), `datasheet` (LCSC's viewer page, or null), `maker_datasheet`, `datasheet_note`, `specs_note` (what the listing leaves out), `spec_evidence` (reviewed maker values, conditions, source), `spec_discrepancies` (catalog/document conflicts; catalog specs still used), `lcsc_url`, `min_order`, `reel_qty`, `has_easyeda_footprint` (null unknown, false none), `easyeda_symbol_uuid`, `easyeda_footprint_uuid`. No lifecycle (`part_lifecycle`).

### jlc_get_parts

Up to 50 parts from the snapshot in one tool call, database only; no specs, datasheets, EasyEDA status, live stock or lifecycle.

- `parts` (required): each an LCSC code, an MPN (max 100 characters) or `{"mpn", "manufacturer", "lcsc"}` (max 100 characters each). A valid `lcsc` wins; an invalid one ("N/A") is ignored beside `mpn`. `manufacturer` (compared loosely: "Microchip Tech" = "Microchip Technology") narrows every match step: Comchip's 1N4007-G answers `{"mpn": "1N4007G", "manufacturer": "Comchip"}`. A part number shaped like a listed code (2SC1815's "C1815") needs `{"mpn": "C1815"}`; a plain code no part has is tried as a part number (MPN row, `note`).
- Reply: `data_as_of`, `prices_as_of`, `price_tiers_as_of`, `total`, `counts` (`found`, `gone`, `not_found`, `error`), `results` (one per input, in order), `hint` when any is gone or not found. Each row has `input` (as given; a string over 100 characters, or other input whose JSON is over 200, is cut to 100 characters and "...").
- LCSC code row: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price`, `prices`, `library_type`, `preferred`, `pcba_type`, `category`, `subcategory`, `description`, `no_datasheet`; gone parts with the gone fields. Unknown: `not_found: true`.
- MPN row: matched as `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)` but never by full text, so values ("10k": use `jlc_search`) and numbers only text mentions are not found. `mpn`, `total` (for the maker given), `exact`, `ambiguous`, `results` (first 10 by stock: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package`, `stock`, `price`, `prices`, `library_type`, `preferred`, gone fields), `match`/`matched_mpn`/`note` when inexact. Gone matches answer as in `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)` (counted `gone`), else `gone_matches`. `other_manufacturers` (up to 10): makers with it in stock when the one given has none. No match: `total: 0, results: [], not_found: true`.
- `error` rows: unusable input (a placeholder such as DNP, empty, wrong type, invalid `lcsc` without `mpn`, over 100 characters, control characters, surrogate escape), or `"Database not available"` for that lookup. Call errors: empty list, over 50 parts, invalid JSON, database unavailable.

### jlc_get_pinout

- Arguments: `lcsc` or `uuid` (EasyEDA symbol; `lcsc` wins), `footprint` (default false; needs `lcsc`).
- Reply: `lcsc`, `model`, `manufacturer`, `package` (may be null with `uuid`), `pin_count`, `pins`, `easyeda_symbol_uuid`. Pin numbers and names are the symbol's; numbers match the footprint's pads. `electrical` only where the symbol sets it. `unverified`: LCSC hasn't verified the symbol. `note`: pins named only by number, or a diode/LED-type part whose numbering varies (connect by name).
- `footprint=true` adds `footprint`: name, `source_link`, `pad_count`, `numbered_pads`, `pitch`, `pad_sizes`, `pads` (number, x, y in mm from the origin, y down, shape, size, layer, hole, slot_length); on failure the pins still come, with `footprint_error`.

### jlc_find_alternatives

- Arguments: `lcsc` (required), `library_type`, `same_package` (default false), `has_easyeda_footprint` (true/false filter), `min_stock` (default 10), `limit` (per list, default 10, 1-50), `board_quantity`, `placements_per_board` (default 1, max 1,000,000), `land_compatible` (default false).
- Reply: `original`, `search_criteria`, `summary`; part types with rules add `alternatives`, `unverified_alternatives`, `comparison` (`original`, `recommended`, `savings`), `confidence` (`level` high/medium/low, `reason`, `unchecked_requirements`); others `similar_parts` and `manual_comparison`. Rows: `score`, `score_breakdown`, `specs_verified`, `specs_unparseable`, `unchecked_requirements`, where they apply `verification_status`, `unverified_requirements`, `moq_warning`, `package_warning`.
- `alternatives` (`summary.found`): primary value and required specs match (connector series and contacts, transistor polarity, regulator output and listed input range; a single input rating checks the maximum only) and readable ratings are equal or better; basic/preferred first. Unreadable ratings are in `specs_unparseable`, not disqualifying. Always check pinout and external circuit; lifecycle isn't checked (`part_lifecycle`).
- `unverified_alternatives`: a required match missing or ratings not comparable (inductor Isat, DCR, thermal current, multi-diode current). Compare by hand; not used for `savings`.
- `similar_parts` (types without rules): RF parts by `frequency_coverage` of the original's range; others with the same package and family first, `likely_drop_in` (pinout unchecked).
- `has_easyeda_footprint` checks at most `min(2 * limit, 15)` eligible candidates, leaving out unknowns (`summary.footprint_filter`). `no_fee` with no match: `summary.extended_examples`.
- `land_compatible=true` (board already made): compares the top 30 candidates' EasyEDA pads with the original's; `land`: `fits` (same pad count and kinds, centres within 0.15 mm), `turn` (0/90/180/270 degrees counter-clockwise, top view; non-zero changes pick-and-place rotation), `max_offset_mm`, `renumbered` (original pad -> candidate pad; check both datasheets). Order: fits as drawn, renumbered, turned, pad 1 moved, not compared (`land: null`), no fit. Pin functions aren't compared. `summary.stages.land` counts outcomes; `summary.land_note` explains. Without it, connectors list `land pattern and pin 1 position` as unchecked.
- `summary.stages`: counts per stage (retrieval, with `error` "retrieval_failed" per failed source; primary; specs; eligibility; footprints; land; output).
- `comparison.savings`: `order_total = assembly_fee + unit_price_diff_at_quantity * component_quantity` (`board_quantity * placements_per_board`), from `original_unit_price_at_quantity` and `replacement_unit_price_at_quantity`; `unit_price_diff` is at qty 1. `price_basis` "price breaks at component_quantity" when both parts have tiers and the quantity reaches a break above either's first (each its largest break at or below it, or qty-1 `price` below its second; `price_tiers_as_of` dates the replacement's), else "qty 1". `order_total` null when a price is unknown. Ranking uses qty 1. `assembly_fee` uses a rounded $3 Economic estimate per extended type (`is_estimate`, `assembly_service_assumption`), not a quote; Standard assembly differs.

### jlc_search_help

- No arguments: `categories` (`id`, `name`, `count`, `subcategory_count`).
- `category` (name or ID): `category_id`, `category_name`, `subcategories` (`id`, `name`, `count`).
- `subcategory` (name or ID; wins): `subcategory_id`, `subcategory_name`, `category_name`, `sample_size`, `attributes` (`name`, `alias`, `type`, `count`, `example_values`, `values` (max 50), `min`, `max`, `total_unique`, `sort_spec`), from up to 1,000 parts.
- Unknown: `error`, `hint`.

### mouser_get_part

- `part_number` (required, max 500 characters): a Mouser PN or MPN (3-40 characters), or up to 10 joined by "|" ("595-LM358P|NE555P"): one request for those not kept (see Quotas). A broad number can fill Mouser's 50-result reply: the numbers it crowded out are asked once more without it, and any still missing are in `not_found` (not kept: asked again next call).
- Matching is loose: batch full part numbers, match results by `requested`/`matched_by`, check `manufacturer`. JST's `(LF)`/`(SN)` endings are optional; other bracketed endings (`(UMW)`, Hirose `(50)`) must match.
- Reply: `results` (grouped by number asked), `total`, `observed_at` (oldest answer used), `not_found` (unmatched or not sent), `not_sent` (`{number: reason}`), `lookup_failed` (numbers Mouser gave an error for). A shared limit holding back some numbers: kept results, `not_checked` (the rest), `retry_after` (seconds); with none kept, the limit `error`.
- Result: `source`, `part_number`, `mfr_part_number`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `category`, `stock`, `price`, `price_breaks` (`qty`, `price`, `currency`), `datasheet_url`, `product_url`, `rohs`, `lifecycle`, `lifecycle_status`, `parameters`, `min_qty`, `currency`, `unit_weight_g`, `requested`, `matched_by`.
  - `lifecycle`: Mouser's status, null for most parts. `lifecycle_status`: Not Recommended for New Designs `nrnd`, End of Life `last_time_buy`, Obsolete `obsolete`; null, New Product, New at Mouser `active`; else (Discontinued) `unknown`.
  - `requested`: the number (trimmed) the result answers (the first, when two name it: `595-LM358P|LM358P`); null when it can't be put down to one.
  - `matched_by` (first that applies): `exact` (MPN, ignoring case), `separators` (also ignoring `-`, space, `_`, `/`), `packing` (JST endings), `mouser_pn`: the part asked for. `prefix` (starts with the number: LM358PE4 for LM358P), `other` (Mouser's own match): check them.

### digikey_get_part

- `product_number` (required, max 500 characters): one DigiKey PN or full MPN; one keyword search each (a partial number can find nothing and still uses a request). JST's `(LF)`/`(SN)` endings are optional (`matched_by` then `packing`; `mfr_part_number` is DigiKey's spelling).
- Reply: `results` (each maker's listing, most stock first), `total`, `observed_at`. Results: Mouser's fields except `unit_weight_g`; `price_breaks` are `qty`, `price` in `currency`; `matched_by` has `digikey_pn` (the result's `part_number`) for `mouser_pn`, and `other` is a listing DigiKey called exact whose MPN and PN both differ.
  - `part_number`, `price`, `price_breaks`, `min_qty`: one packaging's (the PN given, else the smallest order), named by `packaging`; `other_packaging` (`part_number`, `packaging`, `min_qty`, `price`) lists the rest; `reel_fee`/`marketplace` where they apply.
  - `lifecycle`: DigiKey's product status. `lifecycle_status`: Active `active`, Not For New Designs `nrnd`, Last Time Buy (or end of life still marked Active) `last_time_buy`, Obsolete `obsolete`, else (Discontinued at Digi-Key) `unknown`. `last_buy_date`: YYYY-MM-DD.
- Miss: `{error: "Part not found: ...", hint}` (suggests a DigiKey PN unless the input ends in `-ND`), plus `not_sent`.

### part_lifecycle

Lifecycle of up to 50 parts, from kept Mouser and DigiKey readings (see Quotas). Others are asked of Mouser (10 per request), and of DigiKey only when Mouser doesn't list them for the maker given or its daily limit is spent. Only the shared limits cap lookups.

- `parts` (required): `jlc_get_parts`' forms. An LCSC code fills in a missing or unusable MPN or maker from the snapshot (gone parts included); a usable `mpn` wins. `manufacturer` picks among makers sharing a number (loosely). MPNs match ignoring case, `-`, space, `_`, `/` and JST endings; "not listed" holds only for the spelling asked ("LM358P" is still asked after "LM358-P").
- Reply: `results` (input order), `total`, `status_counts`, `retry_after` (the smallest, when any part waited). Result: `input` (as in `jlc_get_parts`), `lcsc`, `mpn`, `status`, and with a reading `manufacturer`, `raw` (the distributor's wording), `source` (`mouser`/`digikey`), `observed_at`, `last_buy_date`.
- `status`: `active`, `nrnd`, `last_time_buy`, `obsolete`, `unknown`, as `lifecycle_status` in `mouser_get_part`/`digikey_get_part`. Mouser listing no status: `active`, `raw` "not stated by Mouser". With both, a stated status beats Mouser's blank, then the newest wins.
- `unknown` adds why: `not_found: true` with `observed_at` (neither lists it), `retry_after` (seconds until a limit allows it; not an error), `lookup_failed: true` (a lookup failed, or Mouser's 50-result cap left it out), `not_sent`, or `error` (unusable input as in `jlc_get_parts`, an MPN with "|", a lone code the snapshot lacks, with `hint`; a placeholder also has `not_sent`).
- `makers`: each maker's reading (`manufacturer`, `status`, `raw`, `source`, `observed_at`, `last_buy_date`) when several makers list the number and none was given (`status`: their common one, else `unknown`), or only other makers do (`manufacturer`: the one given).
- Call errors: no distributor credentials, empty list, over 50 parts, invalid JSON.

#### Numbers not sent

`mouser_get_part`, `digikey_get_part` and `part_lifecycle` send nothing (and spend no limit) for these; `not_sent` names the reason:
- `value`: a component value, alone or with package, tolerance or rating ("100nF 50V 0603"): a number with a unit ("4.7uF"), a resistor code with up to 3 significant digits ("4k7", "15.8k") or a whole number and multiplier with up to 2 ("10k", "2200R"). "1590A", "193M", "158k", "100V" are sent. Use `jlc_search` for values.
- `lcsc_code`: give the MPN, or pass the code to `part_lifecycle` as a plain string.
- `placeholder`: DNP, N/A, TBD and the like.
- `length`: not 3-40 characters (an error in `mouser_get_part`).
- `not_ascii`.

### cse_search, cse_get_kicad

SamacSys ComponentSearchEngine; slow (about 15 s a search, more when busy; cached).

- `cse_search`: `query` (required, max 500 characters), `limit` (default 5, 1-10). Results: `source`, `mfr_part_number`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `datasheet_url`, `has_model` (some ECAD model; formats unconfirmed), `has_3d`, `model_quality`, `cse_part_id`, `pin_count`, `image_url`; plus `total`.
- `cse_get_kicad`: `query` (max 500 characters; the first result with `has_model`) or `part_id` (`cse_part_id`; wins). Needs the server's SamacSys login. Reply: `part_id`, search fields when found by query, `kicad_symbol` (`.kicad_sym` text), `kicad_footprint` (`.kicad_mod` text); either may be null (over 10 MiB is skipped).

### board_search, board_get

- `board_search`: `component` (IC name, max 200 characters; 2+ boards add `consensus`, `pct` of `consensus.board_count`), `query` (max 500 characters; a function: "motor driver"), `tag` (AND, max 10; `usb-c` = `usb`; unknown: `valid_values`), `org` (max 200 characters), `layers`, `limit` (default 10, 1-50).
- Results: `slug`, `name`, `org`, `org_display`, `source`, `source_url`, `format`, `description`, `key_coverage`, `tags`, `key_ics`, `layers`, `width_mm`, `height_mm`, `component_count`, `ic_count`, `matched_by`; plus `total`, `tag_consensus` (one tag alone), `hint` (empty). A `query` with no searchable words (stop words such as board, design, pcb; single characters; quotes and OR aren't operators) browses with the other filters (`note`).
- `board_get`: `slug` (required, max 200 characters), `focus` (max 200 characters: IC name, ref "J1", or value words "USB-C"; returns its pin-by-pin neighborhood), `include_bom` (default false; plain passives too), `include_nets` (default false; full netlist, can be 100 KB+).
- Detail: the search fields (no `matched_by`), `min_trace`, `min_clearance`, `min_drill`, `min_via`, `net_count`. No focus: `components` (`ref`, `value`, `footprint`, descriptions, ratings, and the design files' `mpn`, `manufacturer`, `lcsc`, `mouser`, `digikey` where listed), `neighborhoods`, `passives_omitted`. Focus: `focus` (`ref`, `value`, `pins`), `focus_match_type` (ref/exact/partial), `consensus`, `focus_alternatives`, `power_pins`, `pin_nets`, `pins_in_nets` (its pins in nets), `pin_count`, `nc_pins` (`{}`: all connected) where known. Focus miss: `focus_error`, `available_ics`, `available_refs`. `include_nets`: `nets`, `positions`, `copper_pours`. Unknown slug: `did_you_mean`.

### sensor_recommend

Sensor ICs and modules by measurement, protocol and platform; not for buying (`jlc_search`).

- Arguments: `query` (max 500 characters), `measure` (up to 20, all must match), `type`, `protocol`, `platform` (arduino, esphome, micropython, circuitpython, tasmota, zephyr, raspberry_pi), `limit` (default 15, 1-100). Unknown measure/protocol/platform: `valid_values`; unknown type: no matches.
- `imu`: acceleration, gyroscope or magnetic_field alone; all three in a longer list. Aliases: heart rate/blood oxygen biometric, barometric pressure, lux light, dust particulate, compass magnetic_field. Protocols: i2c, i3c, spi, uart, analog, pwm, gpio, one_wire (`1-wire`), rs485, rs232, can, i2s, usb, ble, hdq, ssi; `gpio` includes analog/pwm/one_wire, `digital` gpio/pwm/one_wire.
- Order: exact ID/alias matches, `platform_count` descending, name.
- Results: `id`, `name`, `manufacturer`, `type`, `voltage`, `datasheet_url`, `platform_count`, `description`, `source_tier`, `measures`, `protocols`, `platforms`, `urls`, and where present `capability_note` (what the part really outputs; other rails), `compensation_inputs` (not measurements), `voltage_evidence`; plus `total`, and `note` when `query` has no searchable words.
- `voltage`: supply volts, "min-max" or one value; versions apart ("3.0-3.6 or 4.5-5.5": pick the one ordered); null without its own supply or a maker source.
- Calculated CO2 (CCS811, ENS160, ENS161, SGP30, iAQ-Core, APC1, SM300D2) is `eco2`, not `co2`; BME680/BME688 IAQ and CO2 equivalent come from Bosch's BSEC library on the host.

### get_design_rules

- `topic` (default ""; truncated at 500 characters): empty or `index` returns `INDEX.md` (every file). Exact keys (`power/ldo`), aliases (`type-c`, `lipo`, `ws2812`), MCU prefixes (`stm32g0`) and category/filename words select files; otherwise the files discussing it most (`note`).
- Reply: `content`, `matched_files`, `topic`. Up to three files in full; more give a key list (narrow the topic). No match: the index, empty `matched_files`.

## Rate limit

- 100 HTTP requests per rolling minute per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64; 1,000 per address in the AI platforms' published ranges (Anthropic's, used by claude.ai and Claude connectors; OpenAI's ChatGPT connectors list).
- Each MCP message (`initialize`, `tools/call`, ...) counts: a stateless client's tool call is about three. `/health` isn't counted. Bodies over 1 MB: HTTP 413.
- Replies (`/health`'s too) carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until your oldest counted request leaves the minute; 0 with none).
- Refused: HTTP 429, `Retry-After` and `{error, retry_after, reason, resets_at, tell_user}` (`resets_at`: when, in UTC; `tell_user`: a sentence for the user). Wait `retry_after` seconds, then resend. `per_ip_rate_limit` and `too_many_clients` refusals aren't counted; others are, so retrying sooner hits `per_ip_rate_limit`. `reason`:
  - `per_ip_rate_limit`: your address used its limit.
  - `too_many_clients`: the server is serving as many addresses as it can.
  - `server_busy`: the database is overloaded; only new `tools/call` requests (or, while busy, bodies slower than 2 s); `retry_after` 2-5 s.
  - `datasheet_rate_limit`: from a `datasheet_pdf` link; at most 20 new links a minute are signed for everyone. Links `jlc_get_part` returned in the last 25 minutes open without one.
- Heavy use: self-host (Source above).

## Quotas

- Mouser and DigiKey daily limits are shared by everyone (DigiKey's resets at 00:00 UTC); at most 25 requests a minute for Mouser, 100 for DigiKey.
- Kept answers are shared and cost no request: Mouser and DigiKey parts 3 days (not found: 1 day); lifecycle readings 90 days (no usable status: a week; not listed: 30 days). `observed_at` dates them.
- Batch Mouser lookups, one DigiKey part at a time, `part_lifecycle` for lifecycle; don't retry a quota error. Self-hosting with your own keys gives your own limits.
